title: Presentability of strongly saturated fixed-source arrow categories
statement: Use presentable infinity categories and universes as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and coherent diagrams, mapping spaces and coslices as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be presentable and $S$ a small set of its arrows. Let $W$ be the smallest replete strongly saturated class containing $S$: it contains all equivalences, is closed under pushouts, is closed under all small colimits of diagrams of arrows in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$, and has the two-out-of-three property for composable arrows. For every object $X\in\mathcal C$, the full subcategory $\mathcal D_X\subset\mathcal C_{X/}$ on the arrows $X\to Y$ belonging to $W$ is accessible and admits all small colimits, hence is presentable. Here $\mathcal C_{X/}$ retains coherent commuting triangles and their higher homotopies, rather than being the undercategory of the ordinary homotopy category.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14, Lemma 5.5.4.12, Proposition 5.4.6.6, and the accessible coslice construction in the first paragraph of the proof of Lemma 5.5.5.14; applied to strongly saturated small generation, not merely to plain saturated generation Read online; not archived in literature/. No matching Stacks tag for this assertion.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A=\mathcal A_W$ be the full coherent arrow subcategory on $W$. By [lem-coef-small-saturated-arrow-accessibility], it is accessible and its inclusion preserves all small colimits. By the objectwise arrow-colimit assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], source evaluation $p:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ preserves all small colimits: first include in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$ and then evaluate at $0$. In particular it is accessible, meaning that it preserves sufficiently filtered colimits. Smallness of $S$ is used precisely in the arrow-accessibility theorem; no smallness of the entire class $W$ is asserted.

The category $\mathcal C$ has pushouts since it is presentable, and $W$ is replete and pushout-stable. Thus [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-source-fibers] identifies $\mathcal D_X$ with the homotopy pullback of $\mathcal A\xrightarrow{p}\mathcal C\xleftarrow{X}*$. By [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula], the terminal quasicategory is accessible and the functor $*\to\mathcal C$ selecting $X$ preserves filtered colimits, hence is accessible. Both other categories and the functor $p$ are accessible by Step 1 and presentability of $\mathcal C$. The accessible-pullback assertion of [lem-coef-accessible-infinity-pullback] therefore gives accessibility of $\mathcal D_X$. All categories may be large relative to the small-colimit universe, but fit in the larger universe fixed in the statement.

source.place: First paragraph of proof of Lemma 5.5.5.14; Proposition 5.4.6.6; Proposition 4.3.1.12 and filtered weak contractibility

proof.text: Let $K$ be any small simplicial set and $q:K\to\mathcal D_X$ any coherent diagram, written as $\alpha:\Delta_KX\to Y$ in the ambient coslice. Form $A=\operatorname{colim}_K\Delta_KX$, $B=\operatorname{colim}_K Y$, and $b:A\to B$ induced by $\alpha$. Objectwise arrow colimits exist by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], so $b$ is the colimit in the arrow category of the arrows of $q$. Each such arrow belongs to $W$; its closure under all small arrow colimits gives $b\in W$, including when $K$ is empty. Push out $b$ along the augmentation $a:A\to X$. The resulting arrow $u:X\to P=X\amalg_A B$ belongs to $W$ by pushout closure. By [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula], this very arrow with its induced coherent cocone is a colimit of $q$ in $\mathcal C_{X/}$. Since $\mathcal D_X$ is full and contains $u$, the same cocone is colimiting in $\mathcal D_X$: mapping spaces from its vertex to a testing object of $\mathcal D_X$, and the spaces of cocones to that object, agree with their ambient counterparts. Thus every small diagram in $\mathcal D_X$ has a colimit. In particular $K=\varnothing$ gives $A=B=0$, $P\simeq X$ and the initial arrow $1_X$.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.12, with the arbitrary-shape coslice pushout formula replacing its filtered/pushout generation argument

proof.text: Steps 2 and 3 give accessibility and all small colimits of $\mathcal D_X$. This is exactly presentability as defined by [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. The fiber and colimit constructions throughout take place in coherent functor categories, retaining all triangle homotopies.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N4-059f638f7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS. I read the item, all three new nodes, all six cited statements, the parent's two uses of the item and the blueprint ancestor's proof paragraph 2 in full. No changes made. Caveat: HTT and Kerodon are online-only and not archived, and network commands are blocked for reviewers here, so the cited pages and numbers (including the '(3)⇒(1)' label of HTT 5.5.4.14) were not checked against the text. Every claim was instead checked mathematically against HTT 5.5.4.5/5.5.4.14-15, 1.2.13.8, 4.4.2.2, 5.3.1.18, 5.4.6.6 and 3.3.1.7. (1) arrow-accessibility: its W matches the item's W exactly; true; covers variable sources, so it is not the item's fixed-source claim. (2) source-fibers: ev0 restricted to a full subcategory is an inner fibration; pushout squares give the cocartesian lifts; a cocartesian fibration is a categorical fibration, so the strict fiber is the homotopy pullback. The pushout-stability hypothesis is needed: the empty-source class in Set breaks without it. (3) coslice formula: colimits in C_{X/} come from colimits over K^◁, giving X⊔_A B. Checked for K empty (1_X), a point (Y), two points (Y1⊔_X Y2) and a circle (A≄X, which is why only weakly contractible K gives A≃X). Filtered implies nonempty and weakly contractible; the terminal category is accessible. Steps: 1 accessible source evaluation from colimit closure plus objectwise arrow colimits; 2 accessible-pullback hypotheses all met; 3 arrow colimit b in W, then its pushout u in W, colimit in C_{X/}, restricts to the full subcategory D_X; 4 the presentability definition, correctly marked elementary. Item tested on Set with S={∅→*} and S={*⊔*→*}. No duplicates in the DAG (the factorization nodes are ordinary-category; the nerve-contractibility nodes cover only ordinary nerves) or in the blueprint. Searches recorded with all three kinds. Every cited statement is in unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, so no tool_uses are needed. No cycle, no SGA. Cosmetic only: a missing separator in the item's source.place, and coslices are cited to the cocone-category definition, which agrees with the explicit model in the new nodes.

lean.statement: theorem small_saturated_coslice_presentability (C : SSet.{max (u + 1) v}) [Quasicategory C] (hC : SSet.Presentability.IsPresentable.{u, v} C) (S : Set (C _⦋1⦌)) (hS : Small.{u} S) : ∀ (X : C _⦋0⦌), ∃ hD : Quasicategory (smallSaturatedCoslice.{u, v} C S X).toSSet, @SSet.Presentability.IsAccessible.{u, v} (smallSaturatedCoslice.{u, v} C S X).toSSet hD ∧ SSet.Presentability.HasSmallColimits.{u, max (u + 1) v} (smallSaturatedCoslice.{u, v} C S X).toSSet
lean.note: The helper smallSaturatedCoslice is the full coherent subcategory of the existing coherent coslice on arrows in the existing strongSaturation of S. The theorem states accessibility and all small coherent colimits for every fixed source.
